_note: THE ORACLE-DERIVED COLUMN DECLARATION. CLAUDE.md: 'the ledger is double-entry and append-only; balances are DERIVED, NEVER WRITTEN.' The reference oracle (Fineract) does the opposite: it stores a denormalised running balance ON the posted journal-entry row and rewrites it in place, by raw UPDATE ... WHERE id=?, from scheduled job 9, outside the command bus, in a service whose columns the JPA entity does not even map. A Go port that honours the non-negotiable will NEVER write those columns, so it can never match them -- AND THAT MISMATCH IS THE PORT BEING RIGHT. THIS FILE DOES NOT NARROW THE GRADED DOMAIN AND MUST NOT BE READ AS DOING SO: G-12's measurement (A2-29) explicitly REJECTED option (c), 'treat the exposing cells as outside the graded domain', because narrowing the graded domain is a hard `user` gate and because it is not needed -- the cells are reachable only through opt-in query parameters no vector need ever set. What this file does instead is exactly what A2-29 asked for and nobody had built: it RECORDS, machine-readably, which columns were NEVER in the graded domain and WHY, PRINTS that record on every run, and turns A2-29 section 6 item 1 -- 'a ledger parity vector must not set runningBalance=true or fetchRunningBalance=true' -- from a sentence in a gate file into a check on the capture bytes. Loaded by nexus/internal/apps/ledger/conformance/oraclederived.go; every count is pinned in Go; the graded vocabulary is MEASURED from the comparator, not declared.

capture_rule._why: A2-29's section 6 item 1, made mechanical. 'A ledger parity vector must not set runningBalance=true or fetchRunningBalance=true. Any capture that does is capturing a stale, oracle-internal accelerator, not a ledger fact.' Until now that rule lived only in a gate record and in one vector's _note, where nothing checked it. The loader now scans the BYTES of the artefact each vector's provenance cites and refuses a vector whose capture carries any of the field names below -- because their PRESENCE in a response body is proof the opt-in parameter was set.

graded_cells.grades: the number of legs the implementation posted
acc_gl_journal_entry.account_id, RESOLVED by the implementation from the slot code and the product mapping table
acc_gl_account.gl_code of the resolved account (a column of acc_gl_account, not of acc_gl_journal_entry)
the Java placeholder constant this leg arrived through, decoded on the family the accounting rule selects
acc_gl_journal_entry.amount, as an integer count of minor units
the sum of the debit legs, integer minor units
the sum of the credit legs, integer minor units
the input the oracle echoed into errors[0].args[0].value, resolved by selector
that the port refused where the oracle accepted
the recorded marker phrase of the port's refusal

columns.why: ORACLE-ASSIGNED SURROGATE KEY. It is a storage fact, not a fact about the posting. A vector identifies an entry by (transaction_id, leg order) and BOTH of those are graded or gapped as structure, so nothing about the entry's identity is lost by not grading a sequence number the port has no reason to reproduce.
STRUCTURE. The resolved GL account. It is an OUTPUT: the request carries a slot code and the product's whole mapping table, and the implementation must key the one with the other.
STRUCTURE. Debit/credit sense. A port that inverts a leg is caught here.
MONEY. Graded as an integer count of minor units. This is the cell the whole corpus exists for and it may never leave the graded set.

columns.why_no_cell_yet: STRUCTURE, uncovered. Every capture in this corpus is office 1, so a cell comparing it could not fail and would be a control that cannot fail (P-98). Closing it needs a second-office capture, not an exemption. NOTE the same single-office fact is what made A2-29's most striking measurement possible: it observed office_running_balance and organization_running_balance holding -1000000.00 and +1000000.00 on ONE entry in a tenant with exactly one office, where the two are the same quantity by definition.
STRUCTURE, uncovered. Every capture is MNT (G-07 admits only MNT). The currency's minor-unit digits already drive amount_minor, so the currency is load-bearing but not separately compared.

STRUCTURE / TRANSACTION LINKAGE, uncovered. It is the key a vector SELECTS by, so a cell comparing it against itself would be the circularity this schema refuses. A non-circular cell needs an implementation that ALLOCATES a transaction id, which no ported context does yet.

STRUCTURE, uncovered. No reversal vector is promoted. NOTE: `reversed` and `reversal_id` are the ONLY two columns of a posted row the oracle's JPA entity can mutate -- they carry the only two @Setter annotations on JournalEntry.java -- and both move through the command bus, not through a job. That is the difference between a correction and a denormalisation, and it is why neither is in the ORACLE_DERIVED set.
STRUCTURE, uncovered. It is a request input in this schema; grading it as an output needs a path where the oracle decides it.
STRUCTURE, uncovered. Date cells reach the corpus today only through refusal.arg0_value, which is a resolved selector rather than a literal.
STRUCTURE, uncovered. Same reason as entry_date.
STRUCTURE, uncovered. It is a clock-derived business date and grading it as a literal would bake a tenant-zone window into a parity vector (T329).
STRUCTURE / TRANSACTION LINKAGE, uncovered. The port does not yet own loan transactions.
STRUCTURE / linkage, uncovered. Savings is ported-but-disabled under the NBFI licence gate, so no savings capture exists to grade against.
STRUCTURE / linkage, uncovered. It is the payment-type precedence chain that `ledger.slot.resolution` already declares not-graded in capabilities-ledger.json.
Free text. Not money and not structure, but NOT exempt either: an oracle-authored comment is reproducible and could be graded.
Free text. NULL on every row in this tenant, so a cell would be a control that cannot fail until a capture populates it.

columns.why: AUDIT ACTOR. It records WHO recorded the fact, not the fact. A port running under its own identity is not wrong for carrying a different actor id, and matching one would be matching user tables rather than money. Measured 2026-08-29T00:08:40Z: 91 rows created_by 1 (`mifos`), 18 created_by 2 (`system`, the scheduler).

AUDIT ACTOR. Measured: 109 of 109 rows carry last_modified_by = 2 (`system`), INCLUDING the 18 never modified after creation -- so on this table the column is a CREATION stamp on an untouched row and a JOB stamp on a rewritten one, and on its own it discriminates nothing.
AUDIT INSTANT. It records WHEN the fact was recorded. Two systems recording the same posting at different instants have both recorded it correctly.

AUDIT INSTANT -- AND THE COLUMN THE DENORMALISATION MOVES. It is PROVENANCE by nature, but on this table it is ALSO a side effect of the oracle-derived write: job 9's UPDATE sets it on every row it recomputes. Measured 2026-08-29T00:08:40Z: 91 of 109 rows carry last_modified_on_utc > created_on_utc, 18 carry equality, 0 are NULL -- so the column DOES DISCRIMINATE the rows job 9 has touched from the rows it has not. It is given its own row, with its own reason, because a provenance column that a job rewrites is exactly the kind of column that would otherwise be filed under the wrong reason and forgotten.
LEGACY AUDIT COLUMN, DEAD. Measured: NULL on 109 of 109 rows. The live audit pair is created_on_utc / last_modified_on_utc; this one is superseded and never written.

LEGACY AUDIT COLUMN, DEAD. Measured: NULL on 109 of 109 rows. Note the consequence for attribution: job 9's UPDATE does NOT touch it, so the legacy pair cannot be used to detect the rewrite -- only the UTC pair moves.

columns.written_by: scheduled job 9 'Update Accounting Running Balances' -> AccountRunningBalanceUpdateTasklet -> JournalEntryRunningBalanceUpdateServiceImpl.updateOrganizationRunningBalance, raw batched `UPDATE acc_gl_journal_entry SET ... WHERE id=?` at :163-181, outside the command bus. Also reachable by hand through POST /journalentries?command=updateRunningBalance (UpdateRunningBalanceCommandHandler); 7 such command rows exist in this tenant.
columns.why: ORACLE-DERIVED. It is a denormalised running total written IN PLACE onto an already-posted row by a batch UPDATE, from a service the JPA entity does not map. A2-29 measured that it is NOT a cache but a SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH: made to disagree with the derived sum by MNT 2,000,000.00 on this live oracle, surviving four organisation-wide recomputes, and propagating into a freshly computed row because the recompute SEEDS FROM ITS OWN PRIOR OUTPUT (:110-116, :134-141, :194-200). A port that honours 'balances are derived, never written' has no field to put it in -- PostedEntry and PostedLeg carry no balance member of any kind -- and will never produce it. A mismatch here is the port being RIGHT.

columns.written_by: job 9 -> the same service at :163-181 (organisation sweep, which sets all three columns) and :211-217 (per-office sweep, which writes office_running_balance ALONE and sets neither the flag nor the organisation column)
columns.why: ORACLE-DERIVED, same shape as organization_running_balance and scoped per office. The two sweeps writing different subsets of the three columns is why A2-29 could observe one entry whose office and organisation balances describe DIFFERENT LEDGERS in a tenant that has exactly one office.

columns.written_by: job 9 -> the same service at :163-181; it is also the job's own WORK QUEUE -- the date finder at :72-73 selects MIN(entry_date) WHERE is_running_balance_calculated=false, and the job never revisits an entry older than the earliest uncalculated one
columns.why: ORACLE-DERIVED, and it is NOT A FRESHNESS SIGNAL: A2-29 observed runningBalanceComputed:true on rows wrong by MNT 2,000,000.00. Measured 2026-08-29T00:08:40Z, and this is the NEW half T429 adds: exactly the 91 rewritten rows carry TRUE and exactly the 18 rows written by the scheduler AFTER job 9 last ran carry FALSE -- a one-to-one match with the last_modified_on_utc > created_on_utc cohort. Entry 96 (transaction L32, a 12356.34 DEBIT on ASSET account 41, whose derived running balance is 72866.39) is served at the contract boundary by GET /journalentries/96?runningBalance=true as organizationRunningBalance 0.000000 / runningBalanceComputed false. THE ORACLE IS SERVING A BALANCE OF ZERO FOR AN ACCOUNT THAT IS NOT EMPTY, and will keep doing so until job 9's next run. A port that refused to produce that number is right; a port that reproduced it would be reproducing a defect.

Filed as a follow-up, to be declared in this same shape the day a savings vector is promoted.
